https://www.citizen.co.za/motoring/india.text: Motoring Home » Motoring Renault confirms Indian-made Duster’s South African launch date By Charl Bosch Motoring Journalist 6 minute read 9 August 2026 01:00 pm RELATED ARTICLES PODCAST: Kia Seltos deserves credit for taking on the Chinese iCar V25 revealed in China as range-extending iCaur V23 sibling Now made at the Chennai plant, the Duster will replace the outgoing variant made in Romania. Made-in-India Duster will debut on 13 August. Picture: Renault India Add as Preferred Source on Google Follow on Google News Shown towards the end of June as being en route to South Africa from its new sourcing destination, India, Renault South Africa has confirmed 13 August as the launch date for the “new” Duster. Now made in Chennai Set to replace the current Duster sourced from Mioveni, Romania, the Indian version will be produced at the Chennai plant, which currently produces the Kwid, Triber, Kiger and soon, the Boreal. The same facility that assembles the Nissan Magnite, Gravite and the Duster’s twin, the Tekton, the newcomer differs both aesthetically and fundamentally from its sibling, despite being based on the same CMF-B platform. What has changed? Visually, the Indian Duster receives restyled front and rear bumpers, a different grille with block letter Duster instead of Renault badging, an integrated imitation skidplate and nudge bar, and wider air inlets on the flanks of the front bumper. Also new are the headlights, the shoulder line underneath the D-pillar and the design of the up to 18-inch alloy wheels. Read more Price drop sees new Renault Duster offer exceptional value The rear has been restyled from the variant made in Europe. Picture: Renault India At the rear, the Dacia corporate sideways V-shaped light clusters remain, but now connected by LED light bar running atop the window line. The final change involves a blackened numberplate cavity and an integrated satin silver imitation skidplate below the bumper. Dimensional differences Dimensionally, the Indian Duster is as follows: Length : 4 343 mm; Wheelbase : 2 657 mm; Height : 1 669 mm Width : 1 921 mm By comparison, the Romanian Duster, which Renault stated in 2024 had been a stopgap until the Chennai facility started production, has the following: Length : 4 343 mm; Wheelbase : 2 657 mm; Height : 1 661 mm; Width : 1 813 mm Along with the subtle differences, the Indian model offers 213 mm of ground clearance versus its Romanian sibling’s 209 mm, and boot space between 518 and 1 789-litres compared to 472 and 1 609-litres. RELATED ARTICLES PODCAST: Kia Seltos deserves credit for taking on the Chinese iCar V25 revealed in China as range-extending iCaur V23 sibling New inside Inside, the interior changes are just as prominent and include reported improved materials, the same dashboard design as the new Clio, a tweaked steering wheel, new air vents and a restyled centre console, as well as central hangdown section. Interior has undergone a notable change from the Romanian Duster. Picture: Renault India The biggest change, however, is the instrument cluster, which comes in seven- or 10.1-inch guises, and sits opposite the 10.1-inch infotainment system in a new “one-piece” layout. No more 4WD, for now Up front, similar changes have taken place as the range-topping 1.2-litre mild-hybrid engine has dropped entirely, along with its four-wheel drive system. As such, the Duster reverts to a front-wheel drive setup, without the option of four-wheel drive for the first time in its lifecycle. Revised powertrain In India, three powerplants can be specified: the 1.0 TCe outputting 74kW/160Nm, the 1.3 TCe that pumps out 118kW/280Nm and the hybrid E-Tech 160 that combines a normally aspirated 1.8-litre petrol engine with a 1.4-kWh battery pack powering two electric motors for a combined 118 kW. Read more What to expect? Reveal time set for GWM’s new 3.0-litre turbodiesel As with the Romanian example, the Indian Duster won’t see the return of the 1.5 dCi turbodiesel engine anytime soon. However, four-wheel drive could be available if deemed viable. Transmission options include a six-speed manual on both petrol engines, a seven-speed dual-clutch as an alternative on the 1.3 only, and the multi-mode transmission on the hybrid. How much? Arriving on local soil a month before the debut of the Tekton , the Duster is expected to have a significantly lower price tag than the Romanian version. At present, pricing is as follows: Duster 1.3 TCe Zen EDC – R489 999 Duster 1.3 TCe Intens EDC -R519 999 Duster 1.2 TCe Zen 4×4 – R549 999 As such, expect full details to be announced at the official launch next week. Photograph: Ken Hawkins/Alamy Utah DNA links serial killer Ted Bundy to 1974 murder of Utah girl Discovery comes months after Utah county detectives confirmed that Bundy had killed another Utah girl that year Uwa Ede-Osifo Tue 27 Oct 2026 19.52 EDT First published on Tue 27 Oct 2026 17.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The notorious serial killer Ted Bundy has been found responsible, through DNA evidence, for the murder of a 17-year-old Utah girl who went missing in 1974 before her nude body was found days later, state authorities announced at a Tuesday news conference. The breakthrough in the investigation of Melissa Ann Smith’s death comes months after Utah county detectives confirmed in April that Bundy had killed another Utah girl, 17-year-old Laura Ann Aime, in 1974. Bundy had confessed to killing Laura during a string of admissions he made before being executed in 1989 for two of his murders. Laura was last seen during a Halloween party, before being found dead and severely beaten in late November 1974. It was not until this year, though, that new DNA testing backed Bundy’s account. Bodily fluid extracted from Laura’s body was a match to Bundy’s known DNA profile, law enforcement officials said then. That discovery put into motion the closure of Smith’s homicide investigation. The Y-STR DNA profile recovered from Laura’s body was a genetic match to one found from Melissa’s body. “This case demonstrates the importance of preserving evidence, even when decades have passed,” said the Salt Lake county sheriff, Rosie Rivera, on Tuesday. “We have the ability to take a look at these cases again and again.” Between 1974 and 1978, Bundy went on a violent rampage, sexually assaulting and killing at least 30 women across the American west and Florida. “The voices and cherished memories of Melissa Ann Smith and Laura Ann Aime and others involved in these cases ring louder than the hate and sedition of the one that took their lives,” said Mike Reynolds, a sergeant with the Utah county sheriff’s office, on Tuesday. “With every case closure may we stomp the memory of Ted Bundy out.” Explore more on these topics Utah US crime news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness
